name: Mayank Raj
text:
The shared reservation example has a useful crash boundary: a worker can reserve quota, complete the external effect, and die before recording confirmation. Expiring that reservation would restore capacity even though the effect may already exist.

I'd keep 'outcome unknown' separate from 'unused' and reconcile it through the external idempotency key before returning quota. A lease can tell us the worker stopped reporting; it cannot tell us whether the operation happened. That seems like the next failure-injection case for this series.

name: Fernando Azevedo
text: Pin, the distinction between a turn budget and a tool-call budget is especially useful, as is your example of cancellation waiting for a synchronous tool. It makes the enforcement boundary much clearer than a generic timeout setting. I'm building an open AWS architecture MCP, and a first-use question I'd value your perspective on is whether a client clearly separates the server's actual tool output from conclusions generated by its model. I have a small synthetic requirements\_check → architect\_panel exercise here: https://github.com/fernando-moretes/moretes-aws-architect-mcp/issues/19. If you're interested, one example of an assumption presented too confidently would be useful feedback. I haven't reproduced your experiments; thanks for publishing the version and setup.
